title: Promote the same declared job—change targets, not production by hand
goal: Keep one reviewed deployment definition while making environment-specific identities, compute, and destinations explicit.
tag: Certification cycle 1 · focused lesson 4 · deployment and change control
concept:
A touring show uses one script in every city. The stage address and local safety rules change; the actors do not improvise a new ending backstage.

Data-platform promotion should work the same way. Put the job, code artifact, dependencies, and permissions in versioned source. Review one change. Then select a named target whose overrides are limited to environment facts. Editing the production job by hand creates drift: the next deployment can erase the edit, and reviewers cannot reconstruct what actually ran.
example: Job orders-55 uses artifact sha-a55. Dev writes dev.curated.orders on small compute. Production writes prod.curated.orders under a production service identity. A safe promotion keeps sha-a55 and the task graph unchanged. Only declared target values change.

use_case.when: Use declared promotion when the same data job must move through development, test, and production with reviewable differences.
use_case.example: A platform team promotes an orders pipeline across isolated Databricks workspaces or Snowflake accounts after integration checks pass.
use_case.decision: Keep code and resource definitions in source, build an immutable artifact once, declare narrow target overrides, validate before apply, and verify afterward. A one-off console edit is reasonable only for urgent recovery when it is recorded and reconciled immediately.

practice: Toggle declared promotion versus a production-only edit. Predict whether the reviewed definition still explains the running job.
boundary: The Python and browser worlds compare one artifact, one job, and two targets. They do not invoke Databricks CLI, Declarative Automation Bundles, Snowflake CLI, DCM, Git, OIDC, approvals, state backends, account objects, rollback, or vendor APIs.

product_sections.title: Databricks: one bundle, explicit dev and prod targets
product_sections.html:
First-minute product recall: Day19 separated file layout from query behavior. Retrieve which facts may vary without changing business code.

# databricks.yml; not executed in Databricksbundle: {name: orders-55}targets:  dev:  {mode: development}  prod: {mode: production, workspace: {host: https://prod.example}}# databricks bundle validate -t prod# databricks bundle deploy -t prod

A Declarative Automation Bundle is an end-to-end project definition. The required root file is databricks.yml; targets can select workspace and resource overrides. Development and production modes add product defaults, but modes do not replace review, identity, permissions, or post-deploy checks. Deployment executes trusted bundle configuration as the current identity.

title: A semaphore permit belongs in finally—even when the task throws
goal: Return capacity after every acquired path without creating extra permits when acquisition never succeeded.
concept:
A parking garage with two tickets can admit two cars. If a driver leaves through a broken gate and never returns the ticket, the garage slowly appears full even when spaces are empty.

A Java Semaphore is that ticket counter. acquire() removes a permit; release() adds one. Work can throw after acquisition. Put release in finally, but only after acquisition succeeded. Java does not enforce permit ownership, so an unconditional release after a failed acquire can inflate capacity instead.
example: The payment client allows two calls. Request A acquires a permit and throws. Without finally, available permits fall from two to one forever. With guarded cleanup, A returns its permit and request C can start.

use_case.when: Use a semaphore to cap concurrent access to a scarce dependency that lacks its own adequate backpressure.
use_case.example: A Java service allows at most two concurrent calls to a fragile partner API while a larger executor handles other work.
use_case.decision: Prefer a client or executor with a native concurrency limit when available. If a semaphore is needed, bound waiting, handle interruption, acquire before the try body, and release in finally only when acquired.

practice: Switch between missing and guarded finally cleanup. Predict the available permit count after request A throws.
boundary: The Java and browser models use integer counters and a forced exception. They do not schedule threads, prove fairness, model interruption races, enforce permit ownership, call a partner API, or benchmark throughput.

One available permit; capacity has leaked

Why guard release with an acquired flag?
A failed or interrupted acquire must not create a permit it never took
Fair semaphores require it syntactically

Semaphore has no ownership check; application convention preserves the count.
What does semaphore fairness not guarantee?
End-to-end request fairness or freedom from timeouts and downstream overload
FIFO selection at documented acquisition points
A capacity bound
A fair semaphore only addresses its own queueing policy and even untimed tryAcquire may barge.

title: A red error budget must stop something—or it is only a chart
goal: Turn reliability evidence into a pre-agreed action with an owner, threshold, and exit condition.
concept:
A fuel gauge is useful because the driver already knows what to do near empty. A red light with no decision attached is decoration.

An error budget is the allowed unreliability implied by an SLO. Senior technical leadership makes it a control loop: define the window and measurement, agree which launch or change actions happen at thresholds, name the decision owner, and define how normal delivery resumes. The policy is negotiated before the stressful moment.
example: The orders API has a 99.9% four-week SLO and one million eligible requests, so its budget is 1,000 failed requests. At 800 failures, the platform has consumed 80%. A dashboard turns red. The useful policy also pauses risky launches, keeps security fixes flowing, assigns the service owner, and resumes after evidence shows the burn is back within policy.

use_case.when: Use an error-budget policy when feature delivery and reliability work repeatedly compete and teams need an evidence-based tie-breaker.
use_case.example: A shared ingestion platform must decide whether to launch a new connector while recent failures have consumed 80% of its four-week budget.
use_case.decision: Adopt the policy only after product and engineering agree on the SLO, eligible events, exceptions, actions, owner, and recovery rule. A simpler incident threshold is enough for a young service that lacks a credible SLI.

practice: Move consumed budget across the policy threshold. Predict the action, owner, and condition for resuming launches.
boundary: The model uses one availability SLO and a toy policy threshold. It does not choose a valid SLI, account for low traffic, multi-window burn rates, latency objectives, severity, security exceptions, contractual obligations, or organizational incentives.

title: Deprecated MCP features still work—migrate before you remove them
goal: Treat protocol deprecation as a compatibility window, not permission to break older negotiated clients immediately.
concept:
A train station can stop selling a ticket before the last valid ticket expires. “Do not start using this” and “this no longer works” are different dates.

MCP 2026-07-28 introduced a formal feature lifecycle. Roots, sampling, logging, and legacy HTTP+SSE are deprecated, but deprecation is not removal. The announced floor is at least twelve months before removal eligibility, and removal still requires a later specification decision. A harness should stop adding new dependence, warn and measure negotiated use, provide the replacement, then remove only when the protocol and supported-client evidence allow it.
example: Client c55-old still negotiates roots. Client c55-new passes an explicit resource URI. If the server deletes roots on July 29, 2026, the old client breaks inside the compatibility window. A staged adapter serves both, records old use, and gives the owner migration evidence.

use_case.when: Use a compatibility adapter when your agent harness supports multiple MCP revisions or independently upgraded clients and servers.
use_case.example: A platform server moves file scope from roots discovery to explicit tool parameters while desktop clients upgrade on different schedules.
use_case.decision: Stop new adoption, negotiate by revision/capability, measure legacy use without recording sensitive payloads, publish a migration path, and set removal from current specification plus client evidence. Do not keep a deprecated path forever without an owner.

practice: Choose warn-and-serve or immediate removal for an old roots client. Predict compatibility and migration visibility.
boundary: The model tracks one feature and two clients. It does not open MCP transports, negotiate real capabilities, implement roots or resource authorization, verify the future removal date, emit OpenTelemetry, or inspect production client inventories.

title: Shift frequency inside the loop so cavity delay no longer chooses every hop
goal: Understand a new microwave-photonic oscillator as a demonstrated research mechanism, not a ready radar component.
tag: Technology breakthroughs · new peer-reviewed research · November 13, 2026
concept:
A piano with fixed frets can play only its built-in notes. Add a controlled pitch shifter inside the feedback loop, and the next note no longer has to land on the old spacing.

A new Nature Communications paper reports PIANO, a photonic-assisted non-periodic oscillator. Conventional delay-based optoelectronic oscillators couple available modes to cavity delay. The demonstrated system inserts a dynamic frequency-shifting module into the cavity, decoupling the agile waveform from that constraint. The paper reports flexible waveforms, 27 ns switching, phase noise down to −134 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz, and a time-bandwidth product up to 1,440,000 under its experimental conditions.
example: Our teaching cavity has modes every 10 units. Desired hops are 10, 17, 24. A fixed-mode toy rounds to 10, 20, 20. The shifted-loop toy reaches the requested sequence. These normalized values are invented to show constraint versus control; they are not the paper’s measured waveform.

use_case.when: Study the approach when a specialist microwave-photonics team needs agile, low-phase-noise waveforms for radar or communications research.
use_case.example: A laboratory compares cavity-constrained hopping with an internal dynamic frequency shift while measuring switching time and phase noise.
use_case.decision: Treat the result as peer-reviewed device research. Reproduce integration, stability, tuning range, noise, environmental behavior, power, calibration, and system-level radar or communications performance before product selection.

practice: Toggle fixed cavity modes versus dynamic shift. Predict the requested and produced hop sequence.
boundary: The integer toy rounds frequencies to a 10-unit grid. It does not simulate an optoelectronic cavity, phase noise, switching transients, feedback stability, time-bandwidth product, TFLN hardware, radar performance, or reproduce the paper's data.

title: Cancel the old deployment only when every completed step is safe to leave behind
goal: Use GitHub Actions concurrency without mistaking workflow cancellation for transactional rollback.
concept:
Stopping a painter halfway does not restore the wall. The first coat is still there.

GitHub Actions concurrency groups limit running and pending jobs. cancel-in-progress: true asks GitHub to cancel the older member when a newer one enters the same group. That controls workflow execution; it does not reverse cloud, database, or Kubernetes changes already made. Production steps must be interrupt-safe, resumable, or explicitly compensated.
example: Run deploy-54 creates schema version 55, then waits before switching traffic. Run deploy-55 arrives and cancels it. The schema remains at 55. If the new run assumes a clean pre-deploy state, cancellation created a mixed release.

use_case.when: Use a deployment concurrency group when overlapping releases to the same environment would conflict.
use_case.example: A GitHub Actions workflow serializes production deployments for one EKS namespace and shared database.
use_case.decision: Queue production releases when ordering matters. Cancel older CI builds freely when they have no durable effects; cancel deployments only after proving every completed step is idempotent, forward-compatible, or compensated.

practice: Choose queue or cancel for two production runs. Predict which durable schema state survives when the first run stops after step one.
boundary: The model tracks one schema integer and two runs. It does not call GitHub Actions, deliver real cancellation signals, model queue ordering, environment rules, Kubernetes rollout, SQL transactions, cloud APIs, signal handlers, compensation, or race timing.

title: Deprecation says migrate; Sunset says when the resource may stop responding
goal: Communicate an API retirement without confusing a lifecycle warning with a behavioral shutdown.
concept:
A store can announce “we are closing” today and still serve customers until the final date. The announcement and the locked door are different events.

RFC 9745 defines the Deprecation response header. It signals that a resource will be or has been deprecated, but does not itself change resource behavior. RFC 8594 defines Sunset, which can communicate when the resource is expected to become unresponsive. A Link with relation deprecation can point humans to migration guidance.
example: /v1/orders returns Deprecation: @1798761600, a migration link, and Sunset: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 00:00:00 GMT. Existing calls still work during migration. Clients alert their owners and move to /v2/orders; they do not treat the warning as an immediate retry failure.

use_case.when: Send lifecycle headers when a deployed HTTP resource has known consumers that need runtime discovery of a migration window.
use_case.example: An internal order API retires v1 across dozens of services while a portal and ownership inventory track completion.
use_case.decision: Use headers as hints alongside direct owner communication, documentation, telemetry, and a tested replacement. Do not rely on clients to notice headers, and do not set Sunset earlier than Deprecation.

practice: Move the current date before deprecation, between deprecation and sunset, and after sunset. Predict the lifecycle signal and whether availability is guaranteed.
boundary: The model compares calendar dates and assumes a service policy. It is not an HTTP server, Structured Fields parser, HTTP-date parser, client inventory, migration portal, availability guarantee, or enforcement mechanism.
